title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-indicator-history-performance review (PR #231)
description: Non-blocking findings from the pr-reviewer pass on PR #231 (GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators response cache + concurrent OHLCV fetch), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges. Filed alongside a needs_work verdict on the parent task for a separate, blocking Session-thread-safety bug -- these two items stand independently of that fix.

checklist.step: Add a test proving the concurrent OHLCV fetch's documented error-priority behavior (a failing daily fetch's exception always takes priority over a failing weekly one) for the case where BOTH fetches fail, not just the single-sided daily-only/weekly-only cases tests/integration/test_stocks_indicator_history.py::TestConcurrentOhlcvFetch currently covers. The logic itself (daily_future.result() awaited before weekly_future.result()) is correct by inspection, but the task's own decisions entry explicitly claims this both-fail priority and nothing currently exercises it.

Reconsider (or at least soften the docstring for) the same-calendar-day IndicatorHistoryResponse cache's interaction with GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis: once the response cache serves a same-day hit, it can keep returning a signal computed from an earlier-in-the-day OHLCV snapshot even after the underlying ohlcv_cache row it derived from is refreshed later that day (e.g. today's daily bar settling after market close, or another endpoint's request refreshing the raw OHLCV cache). get_indicator_history's own updated docstring still states 'The last entry in points always matches GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis's signal/confidence/indicators for this same ticker at the same date' as an unconditional invariant, which is no longer strictly true whenever the response cache is serving a hit. Either caveat that docstring sentence (and docs/architecture/API.md's mirrored text) to note the same-day-cache exception, or invalidate the response cache when the underlying OHLCV data it was computed from has since been refreshed.
